result.final_text:
## What this letter says

You had an appointment on 19 October 2026.
At this appointment, you and your team agreed on a plan.
Your antidepressant is being changed.
This is because of side effects.
You will slowly stop sertraline.
Then you will start a new medicine called mirtazapine.
The letter also gives the date of your next appointment.

## What you need to do

1. From Monday 26 October 2026, take less sertraline. Take 50 milligrams once a day for 7 days. Before, you took 100 milligrams.
2. On Monday 2 November 2026, stop sertraline.
3. From Monday 2 November 2026, start mirtazapine. Take 15 milligrams once a day at night.
4. Avoid alcohol.
5. Do not drive if you feel drowsy (sleepy).
6. Go to your next appointment with Nurse Obi. It is on Monday 16 November 2026 at 14:00.

## Dates and medicines

**Dates**
- 19 October 2026: this is the appointment where you agreed to the change.
- Monday 26 October 2026: take less sertraline. Take 50 milligrams once a day for 7 days.
- Monday 2 November 2026: stop sertraline.
- Monday 2 November 2026: start mirtazapine 15 milligrams once a day at night.
- Monday 16 November 2026 at 14:00: your next appointment with Nurse Obi.

**Medicines**
- Sertraline: your dose goes down from 100 milligrams to 50 milligrams. Take it once a day for 7 days. This starts on Monday 26 October 2026.
- Sertraline: stop it on Monday 2 November 2026.
- Mirtazapine: this is a new medicine. Take 15 milligrams once a day at night. Start on Monday 2 November 2026. It can make you sleepy. This is more likely at the start.

## Questions to ask your doctor

- What does the word "antidepressant" mean?
- What side effects should I tell you about?
- What should I do if I forget a dose?
- What will happen at my appointment with Nurse Obi?

## When to get urgent help

- If you feel worse, contact the team on 01632 960 999. You can call Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 17:00.
- If you have thoughts of harming yourself, contact the team on 01632 960 999. You can call Monday to Friday, 9:00 to 17:00.
- At any time, you can call NHS 111. Choose the mental health option.
- At any time, you can also call Samaritans on 116 123.
- In an emergency, call 999.

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
